findings.expected: First-run examples in getting-started/quick-start/README/running-pipelines match the published persistence-profile contract and the cheatsheet first-live-run command.
findings.actual: getting-started.md:217, quick-start.md:108, README.md running examples, and running-pipelines.md:75 use `bioetl run --pipeline chembl_activity --limit 100` without the opt-down. cheatsheets/cli-commands.md:114-118 requires `--required-persistence-profile degraded_observable` for first live-run. src/bioetl/infrastructure/config/_pipeline_settings.py:32 defaults required_persistence_profile to replay_ready; _run_manifest_builder_policy.py:183-188 fail-closes when exact_replay_capability is missing.

findings.observation: Contributor Quick Start Windows fallback uses `.venv` and extras `[dev,tests]`, which contradicts the mixed Windows+WSL contract (`.venv-win`, tracing extras) in README and getting-started.
findings.method: Inspection of CONTRIBUTING vs README Mixed Windows + WSL section and getting-started 2.2/2.3
findings.expected: Windows contributor fallback uses `.venv-win` and the documented extra set (at least dev,tests,tracing; tests_full for architecture/coverage).
findings.actual: .github/CONTRIBUTING.md:12-13 comments `.venv/Scripts/python.exe -m pip install -e .[dev,tests]`. README.md:201 and getting-started.md:128 specify `.venv-win` and warn that a Linux `.venv` is invalid in PowerShell.
findings.impact: Windows contributors following CONTRIBUTING can install into the wrong venv and miss tracing/tests_full extras, then hit `make lint && make test` failures.
findings.root_cause: CONTRIBUTING Quick Start was not updated when mixed-checkout venv split landed.
findings.remediation: Replace the Windows fallback with `py -3.12 -m venv .venv-win` / `.\.venv-win\Scripts\python.exe -m pip install -e ".[dev,tests,tracing]"` (or point to setup_env_windows.ps1). Keep uv path as primary.
validation: Diff .github/CONTRIBUTING.md Quick Start against README.md Mixed Windows + WSL Development
findings.automation: Docs bootstrap golden snippets test for .venv-win on Windows fallbacks.

findings.observation: quick-start.md labels `uv sync --extra dev --extra tests --extra tracing` as canonical while also saying canonical bootstrap is `make install`, whose extras are `dev,tests,tests_full,export`.
findings.method: Inspection of quick-start Option A vs Makefile install target vs TOOLS.md extra table
findings.expected: A single named bootstrap extra-set, with other extra-sets labeled as specialized (docs, coverage, export).
findings.actual: quick-start.md:45 uses tracing extras; line 51 says canonical is uv sync / make install / setup-plugins. Makefile:99 is `uv sync --extra dev --extra tests --extra tests_full --extra export`. README.md:172 acknowledges the difference; getting-started.md:64 uses make install as the CI/single-OS canonical aggregate.
findings.impact: Operators cannot tell which extra-set is required for a clean checkout; architecture/coverage paths fail if tracing-only bootstrap is used then `make test` is run.
findings.root_cause: Multiple 'canonical' labels for two intentional extra-sets.
findings.remediation: In quick-start.md, stop calling both Option A and make install 'canonical'. Point Option A to TOOLS.md bootstrap row and make install to the operator aggregate with tests_full+export.
validation: Compare docs/03-guides/quick-start.md:45-51 with Makefile:98-99 and docs/00-project/TOOLS.md:43-45
findings.automation: Snippet linter: fenced uv sync extras must match a named row in TOOLS.md.

findings.observation: `make lint` (the CONTRIBUTING/cheatsheet check) runs a weaker mypy/ruff surface than README verify and CI type-checking.yml.
findings.method: Inspection of Makefile lint vs README Verify Installation vs .github/workflows/type-checking.yml
findings.expected: Documented contributor lint command matches the CI strict mypy gate and README verify block.
findings.actual: Makefile:107-109: `ruff check src tests scripts` then `mypy src/bioetl` (no --strict, no format check). README.md:313-315 and type-checking.yml:94: `mypy --config-file pyproject.toml --strict --no-incremental src/bioetl` plus README `ruff check .` and `ruff format --check .`.
findings.impact: Contributors following CONTRIBUTING `make lint && make test` can pass locally and fail the CI strict mypy/format gates.
findings.root_cause: Makefile lint was not aligned with the strict type-checking workflow.
findings.remediation: Either tighten Makefile lint to the CI mypy/ruff format command, or document `make lint` as a fast subset and point contributors to the CI-equivalent command in README/docs-verification.
validation: Diff Makefile lint recipe with .github/workflows/type-checking.yml mypy invocation
findings.automation: CI job that asserts Makefile lint flags include --strict --no-incremental or a documented alias.

evidence.observation: lint: ruff check src tests scripts; mypy src/bioetl
